Text: The cephalic (skull) division of the axial skeleton is made of the {{c1::cranial bones}}, the {{c1::facial bones}}, the {{c1::auditory ossicles}}, and the {{c1::hyoid}}.
Back Extra: Why: the cranial bones box in the brain, the facial bones frame the face, the six tiny ossicles carry sound across the middle ear, and the hyoid anchors the tongue.

Text:
The six cranial bone types, remembered as PEST-OF:

{{c1::Parietal::P}}

{{c1::Ethmoid::E}}

{{c1::Sphenoid::S}}

{{c1::Temporal::T}}

{{c1::Occipital::O}}

{{c1::Frontal::F}}
Back Extra: Why: together they form the braincase: frontal (forehead), parietals (roof and upper sides), temporals (sides around the ears), occipital (back and base), and the sphenoid and ethmoid (the floor, behind and between the eyes).

Text: The cranium has {{c1::8::number of bones}} bones, because the {{c2::parietal}} and {{c2::temporal}} bones come in left and right pairs.
Back Extra: Why: six bone types with two of them doubled (6 + 2 = 8). The frontal, occipital, sphenoid, and ethmoid are single bones that cross the midline.

Text: The only two UNPAIRED facial bones are the {{c1::mandible}} and the {{c1::vomer}}.
Back Extra: Why: both sit exactly on the midline (the mandible is one U-shaped jawbone and the vomer is one thin blade in the nasal septum), so there is no left and right copy.

Text: Four skull bones hold the paranasal sinuses: the {{c1::frontal}}, {{c1::ethmoid}}, {{c1::sphenoid}}, and {{c1::maxillary}} bones.
Back Extra:
Why: the mucus-lined air pockets drain into the nasal cavity, which is why a cold or allergy can cause sinus pressure and sinus headaches.

Pitfall: the mastoid process of the temporal bone also holds air cells, but it is not one of the four paranasal sinus bones.

Back Extra: Why: hollow, air-filled bone weighs far less than solid bone, and the air spaces act like the body of a guitar, amplifying and coloring the voice.

Text: The mental foramen is an opening in the {{c1::mandible::bone}}.
Back Extra: Why: the mental foramen sits on the front of the jaw below the premolars and lets nerves and blood vessels out to the skin and muscles of the chin and lower lip.

Back Extra: Why: the supraorbital foramen sits on the upper rim of the eye socket (supra-orbital) and lets nerves and vessels reach the forehead. In about three of four people it is an open notch rather than a closed hole.

Text: The zygomatic arch is formed by the temporal process of the {{c1::zygomatic::bone}} bone joining the zygomatic process of the {{c1::temporal::bone}} bone.
Back Extra:
Why: each process is named for the bone it reaches toward, so the names cross over; the two meet in the middle to make the cheekbone arch.

Cue: you can feel the arch just in front of your ear.

Text: The hyoid is said to 'float' in the neck because it {{c1::does not articulate with any other bone}}.
Back Extra: Why: instead of a joint, it is slung in place by ligaments and muscles, which is what lets it rise and fall when you swallow.

Text: In anatomy, {{c1::cornu}} means {{c2::horn}}.
Back Extra:
Why: anatomists named the hyoid's slender projections cornua because they stick up and back from its body like a pair of horns.

Ex: the hyoid has greater and lesser cornua, and the sacrum and coccyx have cornua too.

Cue: Latin cornu, as in unicorn.

Text:
Three of the PAIRED facial bones sit between and beside the eye sockets:

{{c1::nasal bones}}

{{c1::lacrimal bones}}

{{c1::zygomatic bones}}
Back Extra:
Why: each sits off the midline with a mirror twin on the other side, so each counts twice toward the 14 facial bones.

Roster: paired = nasal, lacrimal, zygomatic, maxillae, palatine, inferior nasal conchae · unpaired = mandible, vomer

Text:
Three of the PAIRED facial bones build the upper jaw, the hard palate, and the side walls of the airway inside the nose:

{{c1::maxillae}}

{{c1::palatine bones}}

{{c1::inferior nasal conchae}}
Back Extra:
Why: the right and left maxillae and palatine bones meet at the midline to build one hard palate, and each side of the airway gets its own concha.

Roster: paired = nasal, lacrimal, zygomatic, maxillae, palatine, inferior nasal conchae · unpaired = mandible, vomer
